passage:
During a strong wind, May's umbrella turned inside out. She tried to fix it, but the wind pulled it again and again.
A man at the bus stop said, "Point it into the wind first."
May did as he said. The umbrella became easier to control. It still shook, but it did not break.
The man explained that fighting the wind from the wrong direction only made things worse.
Later that day, May thought about his words during a group project. She and her partner had been arguing. Instead of pushing her own idea harder, she asked what problem they were really trying to solve.
The project became easier. May learned that some advice works for more than umbrellas.
